sections.h2: Where do Tazewell County property tax offices work?
sections.html:
Tazewell County keeps its tax offices together in the McKenzie Building at 11 South Fourth Street in Pekin, ZIP 61554. The Treasurer and Collector is in Suite 308 at 309-477-2284. The Assessment Office and the Board of Review share Suite 410, at 309-477-2275 and 309-477-2277. The treasurer and the board both keep weekday hours from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Each office answers a different question:

  • Treasurer: where to pay, what is owed, tax sale information.
  • Assessment Office: homestead exemption forms, senior freeze renewals, name and address changes, and township assessor contacts.
  • Board of Review: written appeals of an assessed value.

The Assessment Office suggests filing a first homestead exemption in person so staff can check the information. It also notes that its senior freeze mailing reflects a higher income limit of $75,000.

sections.h2: What is Tazewell County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Tazewell County sits on the Illinois River in the Peoria metro area, and most of its people live along the western edge. Pekin is the seat and largest city. The county was carved out of Peoria County in 1827, and its seat moved from Mackinaw to Pekin, then to Tremont, and finally back to Pekin in 1849.

It covers 658 square miles. The 2020 census counted 131,343 people, with a 2025 estimate of 130,049. There are 58,550 housing units, 7.8 percent of them vacant, and 75.7 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. About 78 percent of residents live in urban areas.

School districts shape buyer interest here. Pekin Community High School District 303, Washington District 308 and East Peoria District 309 are the secondary districts, while Morton Community Unit District 709, Eureka Unit District 140 and Tremont District 702 are among the K-12 districts. Peoria's CityLink buses run six routes into the county, and three state fish and wildlife areas (Spring Lake, Powerton Lake and Mackinaw River) lie inside its borders. Pekin's January averages run from a low of 14 degrees to a July high of 86.

sections.h2: When are Tazewell County real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the Treasurer set June 1 for the first installment and September 1 for the second. The page states that payments must be received by those dates, with interest of 1-1/2 percent per month if not. A bill that arrives late or never arrives does not relieve the owner of the penalty.

Tazewell County Treasurer schedule for 2025 taxes payable in 2026

June 1, 2026First installment due

The treasurer reports that collections for 2025 exceeded 301 million dollars, which the office disburses to the units of government on each bill. The detailed payment notes are printed on the back of the bill, and written questions to the office are answered by return mail.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Tazewell County tax bill?
sections.html:
The treasurer takes payments at the counter, by mail and electronically. Checks go to Tazewell County Treasurer, 11 S. Fourth St., Suite 308, Pekin, IL 61554. Electronic payments run by phone at 1-309-925-0025 or online with American Express, MasterCard, Discover, Visa, debit cards, PayPal or e-check.

  • Cards and debit carry a convenience fee of 2.25 percent of the taxes paid, with a $1.95 minimum per transaction.
  • E-checks carry a flat $1.25 fee.
  • The provider keeps the fee. None of it goes to Tazewell County.
  • You need the 12-digit parcel number from the top right corner of the bill.

If you cannot find the number, call 309-477-2284 for help. The same fees apply to card payments made at the counter.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Tazewell County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the township or county assessor, because a mistake caught early may be fixed without a formal appeal. If that fails, you file a written complaint with the Board of Review. For the 2026 assessment year, the county's posted appeal filing deadline was September 11, 2026, and it has passed. Under state law (35 ILCS 200/16-55), the clock is 30 calendar days after publication of the assessment list.

The Board of Review is a three-member panel appointed by the County Board, and it sits from the first Monday of June through December 31. It deals only with assessed valuations before equalization, not the tax rate or the bill. The county says a formal appeal needs one of four grounds:

  • The assessor's market value is higher than actual market value, shown by a recent open-market purchase or an appraisal.
  • The assessment is a higher share of market value than the township or county median level in a sales ratio study.
  • The assessment rests on wrong facts, such as a mismeasured lot or building.
  • Similar neighboring properties are assessed lower.

Useful evidence includes the property record card, photographs, comparable sales, an appraisal and a copy of the Form PTAX-203 transfer declaration. Once the tax bill arrives, the county warns, it is generally too late to appeal that year's assessment. A disagreement with the board's ruling can go to the state Property Tax Appeal Board or to circuit court.

sections.h2: What does the Tazewell County Assessment Office handle besides values?
sections.html:
The office posts forms for several exemptions and relief programs. The list covers Disabled Persons (form 343, with a physician's statement on 343A), Disabled Veterans (342), Returning Veterans (341) and Solar Assessment (330). Annual renewal forms and a Disaster Proclamation form (245) are posted as well.

Owners can also request a name or address change, a split or a combination of parcels. Fraternal and veterans organizations have freeze forms of their own.

The office explains equalization this way: a uniform percentage increase or decrease applied to areas or classes of property so that assessments average 33.33 percent of market value. Both local assessment officials and the Illinois Department of Revenue take part. Township assessors hold the local detail, and the county page links to a directory of them.

sections.h2: What happens if Tazewell County taxes are not paid?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes are sold to registered tax buyers at the annual sale, which for 2026 was set for Monday, October 19. The buyer adds interest and penalty, and the county posts tax buyer registration forms and sale results on the treasurer's page.

The sale transfers a lien. It does not transfer the house. State law gives the owner time to redeem, which is 3 years from the date of sale for certificates issued on or after January 1, 2024, with some exceptions for vacant property. Interest on a late installment follows 35 ILCS 200/21-15, 1 1/2 percent per month or portion of a month for a county this size.

When a lender holds escrow money and the taxes go late through its fault, the same section shifts the interest to the lender. Anyone who is behind should ask the treasurer for a current payoff figure and the sale status of the parcel before agreeing to a closing date.

sections.h2: How should a Tazewell County seller handle taxes at closing?
sections.html:
Taxes in Illinois are paid in arrears, so the bill that arrives in the year of the sale covers the prior year. The contract decides how the buyer and seller split it, and the title company applies the split at the table.

  1. Look up the bill with the parcel number and confirm which installments the county shows as paid.
  2. Ask the treasurer in Suite 308 for a payoff if any installment is late.
  3. Ask the Assessment Office to remove your homestead or senior exemptions once you no longer live in the house.
  4. Give the title company the correct tax bill address so later bills reach the buyer.

A Tazewell County house can sell as is for cash, with any unpaid tax cleared from the proceeds.

faqs.q: What are the Tazewell County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the dates were June 1 and September 1, 2026. After each date, interest of 1-1/2 percent per month applies, and the county says late delivery of a bill does not excuse it.

faqs.q: Can I pay Tazewell County taxes with a credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. Cards and debit cards are accepted online, by phone at 1-309-925-0025 and at the counter. The provider charges 2.25 percent with a $1.95 minimum, and e-checks cost a flat $1.25.

faqs.q: Did the Tazewell County appeal deadline for 2026 pass?
faqs.a: Yes. The Board of Review posted September 11, 2026 as the filing deadline for the 2026 assessment year, so that window has closed. Future years follow the 30 days after publication rule.

faqs.q: Does the Board of Review lower my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The board considers only the assessed valuation of the property before equalization. Tax rates and the bill amount come from the taxing districts, and they are not part of an appeal.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about homestead exemptions in Tazewell County?
faqs.a: Ask the Assessment Office at 309-477-2275 in the McKenzie Building, Suite 410. It posts the exemption forms, and it recommends filing a first homestead exemption in person.
